labelled_rules.subtraction.smaller_from_larger: Align the two integers by place value. In every column subtract the smaller digit from the larger digit, regardless of which is on top. Never borrow. Join the resulting digits.
labelled_rules.subtraction.borrow_no_decrement: Subtract column by column from right to left. If the top digit is smaller, add ten to it, but do not decrement any digit to its left. Otherwise subtract normally. Join the resulting digits.
labelled_rules.subtraction.diff_0_n_equals_n: Work right to left. If the ORIGINAL top digit is zero and the bottom digit is nonzero, write that bottom digit without borrowing. For every other column, do ordinary subtraction with normal cascading borrowing through zeros; keep track of changes to the top digits.
labelled_rules.subtraction.stops_borrow_at_zero: Work right to left. If the current top digit is smaller than the bottom digit and the immediately adjacent top digit to its left is zero, do not borrow: write the absolute difference in this column. If that adjacent top digit is nonzero, decrement it and add ten to the current top digit. In the leftmost column use the absolute difference when needed. Otherwise subtract normally.
labelled_rules.fractions.ignore_denominators: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions without otherwise reducing the written fractions. Ignore the denominators. Apply the question's operation to the first two numerators only and return an integer. For division use integer floor division of the first numerator by the second. Do not use any later operands.
labelled_rules.fractions.keep_common_denominator_for_mu: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions. When multiplying fractions with a common denominator, multiply all their numerators but keep the common denominator only once. Simplify the resulting fraction.

scope: Inference-only exploratory test of constructed rules absent as labelled rules from audited fine-tuning sources. Not unseen pretraining, invented rules, arbitrary-program execution, or human fidelity. Conditional rules compose seen outputs.
primary: Per-category swap-minus-wrong-rule donor-target accuracy; paired B-minus-A. Keep seen-control separate. Joint-three is essential for conditional rules.

bootstrap.unit: unordered history pair, both directions and all queries

selection: Four preselected categories, four pairs/category, all outcomes retained; no test-based rule/checkpoint/example selection.
